claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to form and maintain a protective oxide above 900 °C is primarily controlled by the identity of X.
Al-bearing CrFeCoNiX can form a slow-growing, thermodynamically stable, protective Al2O3-containing scale during high-temperature exposure.
Si-bearing CrFeCoNiX forms an adherent, coherent silica-based scale that limits oxygen ingress and suppresses internal diffusion stresses.
Mn-bearing CrFeCoNiX forms less stable oxides that crack or spall because they grow faster, accumulate greater internal stress, and are less coherent at high temperature.
The relevant starting materials are homogeneous single-phase or well-controlled multiphase metallic solid solutions with uniform elemental distributions.
Surface distribution and local enrichment of the oxide-forming element govern oxide-scale coherence, adhesion, and growth rate.
Changing X modulates oxidation through the balance between outward metal diffusion and inward oxygen diffusion.
In Al-bearing alloys, a dense and slow-growing Al2O3-containing scale reduces oxygen transport and provides high-temperature oxidation protection.
Al2O3- or silica-based scales have sufficiently low stress and misfit strain to reduce spallation risk.
Mn-bearing alloys exhibit faster diffusion and form less coherent, possibly volatile or mixed oxides that cause stress buildup, cracking, and spallation.
Al- and Si-bearing alloys will have lower oxidation mass gain than the Mn-bearing baseline.
Al- and Si-bearing alloys will show slower, parabolic oxidation kinetics rather than the more linear kinetics expected for the Mn-bearing baseline.
Al- and Si-bearing alloys will retain more adherent and coherent scales with less cracking than the Mn-bearing baseline.
CrFeCoNiMn is an unstable-oxide baseline characterized by rapid oxide growth, high diffusion rates, unstable phases, and frequent spallation.
The proposed trend applies to homogeneous single-phase and designed multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys exposed to oxidizing or corrosive environments above 900 °C.
Significant processing-induced segregation may change the predicted oxidation behavior.
The minimum Al or Si content needed for protection and the effects of multiphase microstructures have not been quantitatively established.

The hypothesis is falsified if Al- or Si-bearing specimens do not consistently show lower mass gain, slower parabolic kinetics, and better scale adherence and coherence than identically tested Mn-bearing specimens.
